headline: OpenAI adds invisible watermarks to ChatGPT text in the EU
dek: The change covers ChatGPT and Codex in the European Union to meet the AI Act, according to TechCrunch and The Verge.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Watermarking starts in the EU only
body: OpenAI will embed an invisible watermark in text from ChatGPT and Codex for users in the European Union. It reaches eligible users on every plan there over the coming weeks (TechCrunch).
The goal is the EU AI Act, which requires AI-generated content to be detectable by other systems. OpenAI is not making it a global default at launch (The Verge).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: A mark hidden in word choice
s3.body: The technique, called textGrain, adds no visible mark or hidden character. It works on which words the model picks (TechCrunch).

points.t: At most steps several next words are plausible, and a secret key nudges the model toward certain options (TechCrunch).
One nudge proves nothing, but hundreds form a pattern a detector holding the same key can spot (TechCrunch).
Because the signal lives in the words themselves, it survives copy and paste (TechCrunch).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Editing weakens the mark
body: OpenAI is candid about the limits. Short passages, math answers and translated text are harder to detect (TechCrunch, Xataka).
A missing watermark does not prove a human wrote the text, and a match says nothing about ownership or accuracy (TechCrunch).

items.t: API customers anywhere can opt in for select models this week. The setting is off by default (The Verge).
The detection tool is limited to approved researchers and expert organizations, case by case (The Verge).
OpenAI gave no date for a wider rollout beyond the EU (TechCrunch).

caption.hook: OpenAI will embed an invisible watermark in ChatGPT and Codex text for users in the European Union to meet the AI Act.
body: The move comes two months after Anthropic said it would watermark text generated by Claude, also for the AI Act. Anthropic applies it worldwide, while OpenAI starts with the EU only, according to TechCrunch and The Verge.
OpenAI says the watermark does not identify the user, and it published benchmark scores showing similar performance with and without it (The Verge). Outside Europe, ChatGPT output is unchanged.
